messages:
Maria: Heads-up — onboarding Seraphon-7B (open checkpoint) into int4 pipeline. Quick smoke shows long-context QA scores tank after quant + rotary conversion. Suspect head-concatenation ordering (weird interleave) + vocab offset. Posting minimal logs below.

Maria: failing eval: LongQA24h (1000 examples) before quant: F1=0.78 / EM=0.64; after int4+rotary-conv: F1=0.48 / EM=0.31. Perplexity on dev set jumped from ~12 -> ~19.

Alex: ugh. Can you paste the converter flags and the tokenmap snippet you used? Also where did you get the rotary params from — model metadata or inferred?

Maria: converter command: `python tools/convert_seraphon.py --checkpoint seraphon/7b.pt --out seraphon-7b.onnx --rotary-style=headconcat --quant=int4 --vocab-map seraphon-to-unified.json`

Maria: tokenmap snippet:
```json
{"token_offset": 2, "eos_id": 50256, "specials": {"<pad>":0}}
```

Kai: quick thought — headconcat ordering might be (head0,head2,...head1,head3) in the checkpoint but our converter assumes contiguous per-head layout. If rotary angles were saved per-head in that interleaved order, a naive reshape will mix sin/cos across heads and amplify errors in long context.

Alex: can you dump the first 4 rotary angle blocks (fp16) from both original and converted tensors? a diff will tell. Use: `python -c "from tools.dump import dump_rotary; dump_rotary('seraphon/7b.pt', 0,4)` and same on the onnx.

Maria: did that — paste of head0..3 arrays (truncated):
`orig head0: [0.000, 0.017, 0.034, ...]`
`conv head0: [0.000, 0.034, 0.068, ...]`

Maria: conv angles look doubled in stride relative to orig (every value ~2x). also head1 in conv matches orig head2 pattern. so two problems: stride mismatch and head shuffle.

Kai: interesting — maybe the exporter flattened [heads,features] vs [features,heads] and then we applied a `reshape(heads, -1)` which interleaves. Two-pronged fix: 1) detect and correct head permutation by computing cross-correlation between orig & conv per-head angle vectors; 2) detect scale/stride mismatch (probably an accidental freq scaling during quant step).

Alex: try small patch in converter: after load angles do `angles = angles.reshape(n_heads, -1)` then run `perm = np.argmax(np.abs(np.dot(angles, orig_angles.T)), axis=1)` to find mapping; reorder `angles = angles[perm]` and then divide by 2 if cross-check indicates scale. Add a guard to run only if correlation > 0.6.

Maria: ran that locally — re-ran int4 conversion with the reorder+scale fix. Quick eval: F1=0.66 / EM=0.51 (improvement but still below fp16 baseline). Perplexity down to ~13.5. So we fixed most head-shuffle damage. Remaining gap likely quantization noise in embedding projection or normalization folding.

Kai: good progress. Next test: run int8 and bf16 conversions to separate quant noise vs implementation bug. Also run embedding similarity checks (dot product between orig vs converted embedding for 10k sample tokens). If embedding L2 error > 1e-2 we have projection reorder or dtype truncation issue.

Alex: also watch positional/vocab offsets — your tokenmap had `token_offset:2`. Did we confirm that Seraphon used 2 vs our unified 0? Off-by-one in BOS/EOS can create subtle long-context drift.

Maria: confirmed seraphon checkpoint reports `vocab_base=2` in metadata. Converter currently subtracts base but maybe we applied it twice elsewhere. Running a token sanity check now.

Maria: token check quick output: `sample: "Hello" -> ids orig [154,42,7] converted [152,40,5]` so everything is shifted by 2 (consistent). After forcing single subtraction fixed tokens. Re-ran evaluation with both fixes (head reorder+scale + token offset fix). Results: F1=0.71 / EM=0.58, PPX=12.7. Still ~0.07 F1 behind fp16, likely quantization of embed/proj or LN folding as Kai suggested.

Kai: sounds like we narrowed to quantization. Can you run a targeted ablation: quantize only transformer blocks but keep embeddings and final proj at fp16. If that recovers the rest we can add an allowlist for critical layers.

Alex: I'll draft a converter change: add `--fp16-proj` flag to keep projection/embeddings in fp16 and `--head-perm-detect` on by default. Then we can run a canary deploy on dedicated pool `dedicated-seraphon-canary` and run our LongQA harness with 5k samples.

Maria: running ablation now (trained locally): embeddings fp16 + blocks int4 -> F1=0.74 / EM=0.61. That gets within 0.03 of baseline. Good candidate for allowlist.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: service=converter, branch=alex/seraphon-headperm-fix, env=dedicated-seraphon-canary. ETA ~7m :rocket:

Alex: once canary passes (latency + correctness), we'll publish new converter release and update int4 recipes to include `--fp16-proj` for Seraphon family. I'll file an RFC for generalizing head-perm detection.

Maria: filing issue now with logs and experiment attachments. Thanks team.

Kai: nice triage. Follow-up: add a unit test in `tools/tests/test_rotary_mapping.py` that constructs a synthetic interleaved-head tensor and ensures mapping+scale detection recovers original ordering.

Alex: on it. I'll add the test and link PR to the issue.

Maria: ok closing this thread after issue/PR links posted in the ticket. Thanks :)
